rv.q: A young Mexican woman's dream of becoming a bullfighter is depicted in this enchanting fable.
Monet Hurst-Mendoza’s vibrant new play makes its New York premiere at WP Theater.
Apparently, Torera wants us to root for Elena in pursuit of her career.
The world she creates is so evocative and lived in that it transcends many of the coming-of-age drama tropes built into these kinds of plays.

WP Theater’s delightful production of Torera , written by Monet Hurst-Mendoza and directed and choreographed by Tatiana Pandiani, tells the story of a girl in Yucatán, Mexico, who wants, more than anything else, to be a bull fighter (‘torera,’ in Spanish).
Torera is about the cost of breaking tradition and following your dreams; it’s about deep and long-lasting friendship and how culture and tradition can hold us back, even as we honor them.
But Hurst-Mendoza overstuffs the final scenes with too much meat, too many revelations and narrative turns for the characters to absorb — or the audience to swallow.

cn.t: This vibrant family drama about a female bullfighter earns mostly positive reviews for its energy and cultural specificity, though some critics find the plot overly complicated and question the protagonist's motivations.
